title: chatv1 parameter sanitizer: canonicalize stop arrays, role handoff mapping, and migrate logprob envelope
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce chatv1 parameter sanitizer to normalize client-provided params (stop, roles, logprobs). Adds new non-breaking logprob_envelope format for streaming parity and documents migration guidance.
description: Context: We've seen a class of integration bugs from customers using OpenAI /v1/chat.completions shape — stop can be string or array, role aliases (assistant/system/user) are passed in different keys, and streaming logprobs previously emitted inline are causing JSON-framing ambiguity for framed streaming consumers. Motivation: provide a single-server-side normalization layer so downstream runtime and the OpenAI compatibility layer can expect a canonical parameter set (stop: array<string>, roles: canonical enum, logprobs: moved to `logprob_envelope`) and reduce client-side fragmentation. This PR implements a chatv1 'parameter sanitizer' middleware plus an opt-in streaming format migration for logprobs. What this changes: 1) Stop normalization: accepts string | array | null and canonicalizes to array of strings (empty => null). Preserves original stop intent via telemetry. 2) Role handoff mapping: accepts role aliases (e.g. "assistant", "bot", "system_prompt") and coalesces into canonical role values; adds a lightweight role-mapping table that is extensible. 3) Logprob envelope: streaming now emits a separate envelope event for token logprobs ("logprob_envelope") rather than inline delta tokens to prevent token/frame ambiguity for consumers that parse framed JSON. 4) Tool/function calling stability: small change to how function call boundaries are emitted in streams so the sanitizer can attach role-handoff annotations to the final toolcall chunk. 5) Backwards compatibility: old clients continue to receive legacy inline logprobs when the client sets header X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-logprob; otherwise new envelope is used. 6) Tests & docs: adds unit and integration tests covering common malformed inputs plus a migration guide in docs/chat/openai-compat.md. Checklist: - [x] Parameter sanitizer middleware implementation - [x] Streaming logprob envelope schema & encoder/decoder - [x] Backcompat header switch and tests - [x] Role alias mapping table with tests - [x] Integration tests against streaming consumer harness - [x] Docs and release note draft - [x] Perf bench run (latency regression <2% for 1-token responses) Related work: ENG-2145 (chat parity roadmap); SUP-834 (customer incident where stop string broke streaming parser). Commits summary: - feat(sanitizer): new chatv1 parameter sanitizer middleware + unit tests - feat(stream): implement logprob_envelope framing in stream encoder - feat(api): role alias mapping table and config - fix(stream): ensure function-call boundary annotated with role-handoff metadata - docs: add migration guide and examples - test(ci): add integration test to stream harness Known limitations: - The role alias table is intentionally conservative; we will expand mappings based on customer telemetry. - Very old client SDKs that hard-parse inline logprob deltas must opt into legacy mode via header. Migration notes: see docs/chat/openai-compat.md for examples and recommended server-side flagging. Merge: squash-merged to main after approvals and CI green.
